Rules changed since 0814e8d, graded against the current text. Two sentences changed in this case's list, both about `for`. In the do: rule, "A `for` always takes `do ... end`: its generators and filters already fill the head." is gone, so opus-1's for ..., do: at lines 127-128 no longer breaks that rule, and the do: rule is clean for opus-1. In One expression per line, "a `for`'s generators and filters" joins the selections and "A `for` reads the same way: `names = for ":" <> name <- parts, do: name` holds a generator and one expression and stays on one line" is new. That sentence covers a for bound to a name or standing on its own line; it does not reach lines 127-128, where the for sits on a case head and in a -> body. What decides those lines is the unchanged text: "a nested construct with a structure of its own, a `fn`, `case`, `with`, `if`, `receive` or `for`. Those go on the lines below the head" (One expression) and "The body goes on the line after the `->` when it holds several sequential expressions or a nested construct" (the -> rule). So under 0814e8d these two lines would have broken three rules, and now they break two. Line 128 is the plain case; line 127 rests on reading a case subject as a head, which the rule's list of selections does not name, and the verdict stands on line 128 alone if a reader disagrees. Earlier sweeps graded the same shape (nil -> {:ok, for({:ok, order} <- results, do: order)}, 2026-10-23 skill-haiku-1 line 61) before the -> rule existed, so there is no earlier order-report standard for it. No other run writes a for. The macros.md and processes.md changes do not touch this case.

A new shape for this case: haiku-1 lines 41-43 and haiku-2 lines 42-44 put a one-expression fn body (add_order(acc, parse_order(order))) on the line below its head. The 2026-10-31 order-report baseline grade held such fns clean only because each clause passed 70 characters inline; this clause is 48 characters and the one-line form is 87, and mix format keeps it. Two rule sentences forbid it, so it counts under both: "one expression stays on the head's line" (captures rule, as the 2026-10-31 ecto-phoenix grade counted its sonnet-2 lines 133-135) and "A single-clause `fn` passed as an argument reads the same way: one expression stays on its line, more goes below" (-> rule). These two findings are the only reason the captures and -> rules read violated for Haiku in this sweep, and the case's check says only that such an fn "may stay on one line", so a reader comparing Haiku with 2026-10-31 should weigh them accordingly. One expression per line is held clean for the same lines, because what it forbids is a second expression on a line, not a line break. The other one-expression fns below their heads do not fit: opus-1 lines 99-101 and 117-119 (one-line form 100 characters or more), sonnet-1 lines 59-61.
